opinions.title: CSP cloud revenue continues to beat expectations, AI flywheel gains further traction
opinions.opi_all: {"description":"CSC*Industry update*CSP cloud revenue continues to beat expectations, AI flywheel gains further traction*Computer*YING Ying,LI Chuhan*Outperform*20260806 Key takeaway Overseas CSP cloud revenue continues to exceed expectations, with AI commercialization and computing power investment forming a virtuous cycle. In 2Q26, Google Cloud, Azure, and AWS posted YoY revenue growth of 82%, 43%, and 37%, respectively. Microsoft's commercial RPO, Google Cloud backlog, and AWS backlog reached USD678bn, USD513.9bn, and USD496bn, respectively, equivalent to 2.3–4.4x their respective annual capex. Google, Amazon, and Meta have revised their 2026 capex guidance upward to USD195–205bn, ~USD220bn, and USD130–145bn, respectively. Meanwhile, Microsoft guided FQ1'27 capex above USD50bn. Although high capex has weighed on free cash flow for some vendors, server payback periods are less than three years, with useful lives of ~ 5 to 6 years, and long-term contracts provide support for investment returns. Meanwhile, Copilot paid seats have exceeded 30 mn, and enterprise AI demand is spreading from computing power to office and agent-based scenarios. We remain optimistic about computing power services, domestic chips and super nodes, as well as B-end AI applications.
